newsitem.title: UK: Plane Handling wins Kuwait Airways cargo contract.
newsitem.headline: Plane Handling wins Kuwait Airways cargo contract.

text.p: Plane Handling Ltd said it has won a three year contract from Kuwait Airways to handle approximately 10,000 tonnes a year of cargo in and out of the UK.

The contract will start tomorrow, July 15 and will involve Plane Handling undertaking full cargo handling activities from its new on-airport cargo facility at Heathrow, Building 549, a company statement said.

Kuwait Airways cargo sales executive, Rick Snape, said the contract will provide support for the carrier's daily Airbus Industrie A-340 and A300 flights from London, as well as its twice weekly freighter service.
Previously Aer Lingus was providing cargo handling for the Kuwaiti carrrier.

Plane Handling operates 215,000 sq ft of cargo transit shed and office facilities at Heathrow and Manchester airports, handling 130,000 tonnes of cargo annually for some 25 airlines, the statement added. The figure excludes the 10,000 tonnes from Kuwait Airlines.

It is also leasing a further 140,000 sq ft off-airport cargo facility at Heathrow -- opposite the existing facility -- from BAA, which is scheduled to be operational in February 1998, Plane Handling operations director, Pat Heslop said.
He added: "We won't be looking for additional business before (next year's) move, as virtually all the space is now committed and we are expecting a very busy summer and winter period."

Other airlines using Plane Handling included Aeroflot, Air New Zealand, All Nippon Airlines, Eva Air, Virgin Atlantic Airways, Delta Airlines, NorthWest Airlines, Malev, Royal Brunei and Air Seychelles.
